newsitem.title: USA: NZ SPORT - Nobilo in position for top-five finish.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Nobilo in position for top-five finish.

text.p: MAMARONECK, New York, Aug 17 - A fighting, third-round three-under-par 67 has New Zealand golfer Frank Nobilo well positioned for a top-five finish in the United States PGA championship, NZPA reports.
Nobilo jumped 45 places to join a group of nine players in 11th place, only two shots shy of third place.
The championship is set to be a two-horse race between British Open champion Justin Leonard and fellow American Davis Love, who lead by six strokes on 203.

Nobilo's round, equalled by playing partner Scott McCarron, of the United States, and Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, provided the talented New Zealander with the real prospect of snaring a prestigious top-five result.
Nobilo calmly edged his way up the leaderboard on a day of oppressive heat and humidity in the New Your area, conditions that tested the composure of the players.

After two days of mounting frustration, there was a spring in Nobilo's step, enthusiasm in his speech and confidence in his game. While he'd walked a crooked line around Winged Foot in the opening two rounds, today it was virtually a straight line all
the way to the scorers' hut.
"I played great today and it was a big difference compared to the way I played the first two rounds," Nobilo said.

"I seemed to have a habit sometimes of turning a great round into a good one, and today was sort of in between. It could have been a couple better, but I think when you break 70 around here, you've really played well".
The key to Nobilo's good scoring, as opposed to his indifferent first two rounds, was his accurate driving, with Nobilo hitting 10 of the 14 par-four and par-five fairways in regulation.
He also turned around appreciably his statics for hitting greens in regulation, finding 16 greens, compared to just half that number 24 hours earlier.
"I just hit nearly all the greens in regulations and when you do that, you should shoot a good score," Nobilo said.

"But this golf course never lets up because I had a few eight to 10-footers for birdie, and you want to make those so bad because you don't know when you are going to get your next chance, and that's the frustrating thing about it because on an easier golf course, you'd probably knock them in.
"But compared to yesterday, the way I played today was like comparing chalk with cheese, and today is the way I like to play, and the way I know I can."

Nobilo said he and his coach Robert Baker selected a four-under 66 as the figure to strive for today, and although Nobilo was four-under after 12 holes, he fell just one shy of his goal after bogeying the 16th.
But it was a round to give life to the New Zealander's chances of grabbing a top-three finish at best, and at least, a top-five placing.
"I think four-under is going to win the tournament now," he said before knowing the outcome of the day's play.
"My score is probably just going to be two shots too shy at this stage unless I play absolutely fantastically great tomorrow.
"I played great today, but I also left a few out there. I think I can play as well if not better."
